query: For a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix evaluated in sliding from room temperature to 800 °C, what single intervention could overcome the difficulty of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range? Earlier studies of other self-lubricating material systems reported low coefficients of friction at 704 °C and favorable friction and wear behavior over broad temperature ranges. However, these results do not resolve the limited understanding of wide-temperature tribological performance in CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys, and effectiveness must be maintained as operating temperature, load, and environment vary. Formulate one hypothesis that identifies a single intervention without presupposing its class, explains its mechanism, predicts friction and wear relative to the starting CoCrFeNi material, defines its temperature, load, and environmental boundaries, relates it to prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a small, immiscible addition of bismuth (≈3 at.% Bi) into a CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy (HEA) will create dispersed Bi-rich precipitates that extrude to the sliding interface and oxidise to Bi/Bi₂O₃ during sliding. The resulting soft or liquid (T > 271 °C) Bi-based tribofilm will persist from room temperature up to ~800 °C in air, lowering shear strength at the contact. Consequently, the Bi-modified HEA will show a coefficient of friction (COF) at least 30 % lower and a volumetric wear rate at least 50 % lower than the undoped CoCrFeNi alloy over the entire 25–800 °C range under the specified loads and sliding speeds.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy, polycrystalline, grain size ~20 µm, produced by vacuum arc melting and homogenised at 1100 °C/12 h, then air-cooled.
generation.intervention: Add 3 atomic % Bi to the melt before solidification to form a CoCrFeNi–3Bi alloy that retains a single-phase FCC matrix with finely dispersed Bi-rich particles (~0.5–2 µm) along grain boundaries.
generation.conditions: Reciprocating or pin-on-disk sliding against an alumina counter-body in laboratory air (RH 30–50 %), normal load 5 N (contact pressure ≈1 GPa), sliding speed 0.1 m s⁻¹, temperatures stepped at 25 °C, 200 °C, 400 °C, 600 °C, and 800 °C.
generation.structural_mediator: Bi-rich precipitates that (i) are plastic/soft at 25 °C, (ii) melt at 271 °C forming a nanometre-thick liquid interfacial film, and (iii) oxidise in situ to Bi/Bi₂O₃; the tribofilm continuously replenishes from the subsurface during sliding.
generation.mechanism: The low-melting, low-shear Bi phase extrudes under contact stress; above 271 °C it becomes liquid, spreading rapidly and forming a lubricious interfacial layer. Simultaneous oxidation generates Bi₂O₃, which also exhibits low shear strength and good thermal stability up to ~820 °C, protecting the HEA matrix from severe adhesive wear and oxidation. The soft/liquid film accommodates shear, reduces adhesive junction strength, and limits direct metal–metal contact, thereby lowering both COF and wear across the broad temperature window.
generation.predicted_outcome: Average steady-state COF ≤0.30 (versus 0.60–0.80 for the baseline) and wear rate ≤5 × 10⁻⁵ mm³ N⁻¹ m⁻¹ (≥50 % reduction) at every tested temperature between 25 °C and 800 °C.
generation.baseline: Undoped CoCrFeNi HEA tested under identical conditions shows COF 0.6–0.8 and wear rate ≈1 × 10⁻⁴ mm³ N⁻¹ m⁻¹, with strong temperature dependence (lower COF at 400–600 °C due to oxide glaze but severe wear at 25 °C and >700 °C).
generation.boundary: Effective in oxidising atmospheres (air) between 25 °C and 800 °C, sliding speeds up to 0.5 m s⁻¹ and normal loads up to 10 N. Performance may degrade above ~850 °C (Bi evaporation), under vacuum/inert gas (insufficient oxide formation), or at loads causing complete lubricant depletion.
generation.uncertainty: Potential embrittlement from Bi segregation; stability of Bi/Bi₂O₃ film under cyclic heating; evaporation of Bi near 800 °C; exact optimum Bi concentration may differ (2–5 at.%).

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate CoCrFeNi and CoCrFeNi–3Bi alloys under identical processing. Conduct pin-on-disk tests in air at 25, 200, 400, 600, and 800 °C (5 N, 0.1 m s⁻¹, 1000 m sliding distance). After each test analyse wear tracks (3D profilometry for volume loss; XPS/EDS for Bi/Bi₂O₃ presence) and measure steady-state COF.
measurements: Average COF over last 200 m of sliding at each temperature
Wear volume per unit sliding distance
Cross-sectional SEM/EDS of wear tracks for subsurface Bi distribution
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if, at any tested temperature within 25–800 °C, (a) the Bi-modified alloy does not show at least a 20 % reduction in both COF and wear rate relative to the baseline OR (b) surface analyses reveal no enrichment of Bi/Bi₂O₃ on the wear track after sliding.
